name: claude-resurrect
description: Bring back the Claude Code CLI sessions that were open in your editor terminals before a restart.
author: Jakub Michalec <kuba.michalec@gmail.com>

enumDescriptions: Show a list of interrupted sessions for this window and restore the ticked ones.
Restore every interrupted session for this window without asking.
Do nothing on startup. The Restore Sessions command still works.
claudeResurrect.restoreOnStartup.description: What to do with interrupted Claude Code sessions when a window opens.

claudeResurrect.claudeCommand.description: Command used to launch Claude Code in the restored terminal.

claudeResurrect.extraArguments.description: Extra arguments appended after the resume flag, for example a permission mode.

claudeResurrect.shutdownWindowSeconds.description: Sessions interrupted within this many seconds of the last interruption count as killed by the same editor shutdown. Older ones were closed one by one and are not restored.

claudeResurrect.reuseRestoredTerminals.description: Resume a session inside the terminal tab the editor restored for it, when a tab with that name exists, instead of opening a new one next to it.

claudeResurrect.compaction.enabled.description: Compact the event log on startup when it is large and has been quiet. The log is append-only, so without compaction it grows with every session start and end.

claudeResurrect.compaction.thresholdKb.description: Compact only when the event log is larger than this many kilobytes.

claudeResurrect.compaction.quietSeconds.description: Compact only when nothing has been written to the log for this many seconds, so a session starting up at the same moment is never lost.

claudeResurrect.compaction.keepInterrupt.description: Interrupted sessions older than this many days are dropped during compaction.
